cau_hoi: What is the largest hot desert in the world, covering most of North Africa?
giai_thich: The Sahara covers about 9 million square kilometers, nearly the size of the United States or China, spanning over 10 countries. Daytime summer temperatures can exceed 50°C, but at night they can drop sharply due to the dry air not retaining heat. The name "Sahara" in Arabic simply means "desert." If including icy regions, Antarctica is actually the largest desert in the world.

cau_hoi: What is the longest river in Africa (and considered by many to be the longest in the world)?
giai_thich: The Nile River is about 6,650 km long, flowing from the Great Lakes region in East Africa northward, through the desert, and into the Mediterranean Sea. Scientists still debate whether the Nile or the Amazon is longer, as it is very difficult to determine the exact source point. In the arid desert, the green strip along the banks of the Nile supports tens of millions of people.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Egypt?
giai_thich: Cairo is located on the banks of the Nile River, right at the point where the river spreads into a delta. The metropolitan area of Cairo has over 20 million people, making it one of the largest urban areas in Africa and the Arab world. The city is known as the "City of a Thousand Minarets" due to its thousands of mosques. Alexandria is the second largest city, located on the Mediterranean coast.

cau_hoi: What is the highest mountain in Africa?
giai_thich: Kilimanjaro stands at about 5,895 m, making it the highest free-standing mountain in the world. Despite being near the equator, its summit is covered in snow due to its high elevation. Climbing Kilimanjaro, one passes through various climate zones: from farmland, rainforests, grasslands, high-altitude deserts to glacial regions, akin to traveling from the equator to the Arctic.

cau_hoi: In terms of area, what position does Africa hold among the continents of the world?
giai_thich: Africa covers about 30 million square kilometers, making it the second largest continent after Asia, accounting for about 20% of the Earth's land area. On many popular world maps, Africa appears smaller than it actually is due to the way maps are drawn, which enlarges areas near the poles. In reality, the entire landmass of the USA, China, India, and most of Europe could fit within Africa.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Kenya?
giai_thich: Nairobi is situated at an altitude of about 1,700 m, giving it a cool climate despite being near the equator. The city's name comes from the Maasai language, meaning "place of cool water." Nairobi is a major economic hub in East Africa and is home to the United Nations Environment Programme. Mombasa is the largest port city in Kenya, located on the Indian Ocean.

cau_hoi: Which country has the largest population in Africa?
giai_thich: Nigeria has over 220 million people, making it the sixth most populous country in the world, with a rapidly growing population expected to increase in the coming decades. Nigeria is home to over 250 ethnic groups, the largest being Hausa, Yoruba, and Igbo. Nigeria's film industry, known as "Nollywood," produces a vast number of films each year, ranking among the highest in the world.

cau_hoi: What is the largest island in Africa?
giai_thich: Madagascar is located in the Indian Ocean, off the southeastern coast of Africa, separated from the mainland by a wide strait. The island has been isolated from other continents for a long time, resulting in a unique array of flora and fauna found nowhere else in the world. Madagascar is famous for its giant baobab trees and lemurs.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Morocco?
giai_thich: Many people think the capital of Morocco is Casablanca because it is the largest city and economic center, but the actual capital is Rabat, located on the Atlantic coast at the mouth of the Bou Regreg River. Rabat features an old medina and the Kasbah des Oudaias fortress with its white and blue houses. Tunis is the capital of Tunisia.

cau_hoi: Which river flows through the largest tropical rainforest in Africa and has the largest water flow in the continent?
giai_thich: The Congo River is about 4,700 km long, making it the second longest river in Africa after the Nile, but its discharge into the sea is many times greater than that of the Nile, second only to the Amazon in the world. The Congo River basin is covered by dense rainforests, home to gorillas, chimpanzees, forest elephants, and thousands of other species.

cau_hoi: Cape of Good Hope, the famous headland in the southwestern tip of Africa, belongs to which country?
giai_thich: The Cape of Good Hope is located on the Cape Peninsula, near Cape Town. The Portuguese navigator Bartolomeu Dias rounded this headland in 1488 and called it the "Cape of Storms"; later, the King of Portugal renamed it "Cape of Good Hope" because it opened up hopes for a sea route to India. Many people mistakenly believe this is the southernmost point of Africa.

cau_hoi: What is the largest lake in Africa (and the largest tropical lake in the world)?
giai_thich: Lake Victoria covers about 68,800 km², making it the second largest freshwater lake in the world by area, only after Lake Superior in North America. Although large, the lake is quite shallow, with a maximum depth of only about 80 m. Tens of millions of people living around the lake depend on fishing. The lake was named after Queen Victoria of England in the 19th century.

cau_hoi: In which country is Mount Kilimanjaro located?
giai_thich: Kilimanjaro is located in northeastern Tanzania, very close to the Kenyan border. From Kenya, especially from Amboseli National Park, you can take famous photos of elephants walking under the snow-capped mountain. Each year, about 30,000 to 50,000 people attempt to climb to the summit. The name Kilimanjaro may mean "white mountain" or "shining mountain."

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Nigeria?
giai_thich: In 1991, Nigeria moved its capital from the coastal city of Lagos to Abuja, a newly planned and built city in the center of the country. The central location makes Abuja more neutral among the major regions and ethnic groups. The natural symbol of Abuja is Aso Rock, a massive granite rock about 400 m high. Lagos remains the largest city and economic center.

cau_hoi: Which country is the Kalahari Desert primarily located in?
giai_thich: The Kalahari covers about 900,000 km², spanning Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa. The Kalahari has more shrubs, grasses, and acacia trees than typical sandy deserts, so many scientists refer to it as a "semi-arid desert." The Kalahari is home to black-maned lions, gemsboks, and the upright meerkat.

cau_hoi: Which country has the largest area in Africa?
giai_thich: Algeria covers about 2.38 million km², more than 7 times the area of Vietnam. About 80% of Algeria's territory is covered by the Sahara Desert, so most of the population lives along the Mediterranean coast in the north. Before 2011, Sudan was the largest country in Africa, but after South Sudan separated, Algeria became the largest.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Ghana?
giai_thich: Accra is located on the coast of the Gulf of Guinea, and is the largest city and economic, cultural center of Ghana. Ghana is one of the largest cocoa producers in the world, along with its neighbor Côte d'Ivoire. Ghana is also rich in gold and was once called the "Gold Coast" during colonial times. Abidjan is the largest city in Côte d'Ivoire.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the mountain range that runs through northwest Africa across Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia?
giai_thich: The Atlas Mountains stretch about 2,500 km, separating the Mediterranean and Atlantic coastal regions from the Sahara Desert. The mountain range blocks moisture from the sea, so the northern slopes receive rain and can support vegetation, while the southern side is arid. The name of the mountain range is associated with the giant Atlas from Greek mythology, who had to bear the sky on his shoulders.

cau_hoi: Which desert in southwestern Africa is considered the oldest desert in the world, having been arid for at least about 55 million years?
giai_thich: The Namib Desert runs along the coast of Namibia, stretching about 2,000 km. Notably, the desert is adjacent to the sea: the cold ocean current along the coast cools the air, creating fog but almost no rain. The Namib has some of the highest orange-red sand dunes in the world. The name "Namib" means "vast place, nothing."

cau_hoi: What is the name of the rift valley system that stretches about 6,000 km from the Middle East through East Africa, where the African continent is gradually splitting apart?
giai_thich: The Great Rift Valley formed when tectonic plates pulled apart, causing the land in between to sink. Along the valley, there are many volcanoes and deep lakes. Many important fossils of human ancestors have been found here, making East Africa known as the "cradle of humanity." In millions of years to come, the East African region may completely separate into its own landmass.

cau_hoi: Which country is the capital Dakar, located near the westernmost point of the African continent, in?
giai_thich: Dakar is located on the Cap-Vert Peninsula jutting out into the Atlantic Ocean, with the nearby Almadies Point being the westernmost point of the African continent. From 1978 to 2007, Dakar was the endpoint of the famous Paris-Dakar rally, which crossed the Sahara Desert. Off the coast of Dakar is Gorée Island, which was once a slave trading post and is now a world heritage site reminding us of a painful history.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Algeria?
giai_thich: Algiers is located on the Mediterranean coast and is known as the "White Alger" due to its prominent white-painted buildings on the hillside overlooking the sea. The old Casbah district, with its narrow alleys and steep staircases, is a world heritage site. The name Algeria is derived from the name of its capital. Oran is the second largest city in Algeria.

cau_hoi: Which island nation, consisting of 115 islands in the Indian Ocean and having the smallest population in Africa, is it?
giai_thich: Seychelles has a population of about 100,000 and is located approximately 1,500 km off the East African coast. Some of the main islands are ancient granite, remnants of the supercontinent Gondwana, while others are coral islands. Seychelles is famous for its beaches with giant round granite boulders and is home to the giant Aldabra tortoise. The capital, Victoria, is one of the smallest capitals in the world.

cau_hoi: What is the longest freshwater lake in the world (approximately 670 km) and the second deepest lake in the world, located in East Africa?
giai_thich: Lake Tanganyika is about 1,470 m deep, second only to Lake Baikal, and may have existed for around 10 million years. The lake is shared by four countries: Tanzania, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Burundi, and Zambia. It lies in a branch of the rift valley and is home to hundreds of endemic cichlid fish species with vibrant colors.

cau_hoi: In which country is the Okavango Delta, where the river does not flow into the sea but "disappears" into the desert?
giai_thich: The Okavango River originates from the Angolan highlands, flows into Botswana, and then spreads out into a vast swamp in the Kalahari Desert, where water evaporates and seeps into the ground. Each year, floods arrive in the dry season, creating green oases for elephants, lions, hippos, and hundreds of bird species. The Okavango Delta is UNESCO's 1,000th natural world heritage site (in 2014).

cau_hoi: What is unique about the Congo River compared to other major rivers in the world?
giai_thich: The Congo River flows in a large arc: first flowing north, crossing the equator, then turning west and flowing south, crossing the equator a second time before emptying into the Atlantic Ocean. Because the basin lies in both hemispheres, there is always part of the basin in the rainy season, so the Congo River has a fairly stable water flow year-round.

cau_hoi: What record does Lake Malawi in East Africa hold?
A: Has the most fish species compared to any lake in the world
B: Is the largest artificial lake in the world
C: Is the saltiest lake in the world
D: Is the highest lake in the world
giai_thich: Lake Malawi has about 700 to 1,000 fish species, most of which are cichlids unique to this lake. Scientists study these fish to understand how new species form rapidly. The lake's clear water and brightly colored fish make it popular among aquarium enthusiasts. The lake is shared by Malawi, Mozambique, and Tanzania.

cau_hoi: Which two capitals in the world are closest to each other (excluding Rome and Vatican), separated only by the Congo River?
giai_thich: Kinshasa is the capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo, while Brazzaville is the capital of the Republic of Congo; the two cities face each other across the Congo River, just a few kilometers apart. Kinshasa has over 15 million inhabitants, making it the most populous French-speaking city in the world, even more than Paris. Just below the two cities, the Congo River flows through fierce rapids.

cau_hoi: In which country is the Serengeti National Park, famous for its massive annual migrations of wildebeest and zebras, primarily located?
giai_thich: The Serengeti covers approximately 14,750 km² and is one of the most famous wild grasslands in the world. The name "Serengeti" comes from the Maasai language, meaning "endless plains." It has the highest density of lions in Africa. The Serengeti connects with the Maasai Mara reserve in Kenya, forming a unified ecosystem.

cau_hoi: Which country is completely surrounded by the territory of Lesotho?
giai_thich: Lesotho is one of three countries in the world that is completely surrounded by another country (along with Vatican City and San Marino within Italy). Lesotho covers about 30,000 km², mostly mountainous, and is thus called the "Kingdom in the Sky." The people often wear wool blankets as cloaks to keep warm in the high mountains.

cau_hoi: The Ngorongoro crater, home to tens of thousands of wild animals, is located in which country?
giai_thich: Ngorongoro is the largest intact caldera in the world, measuring about 260 km², with walls rising approximately 600 m. Inside are grasslands, lakes, and forests, home to lions, elephants, black rhinos, hippos, and flamingos, forming a closed 'natural zoo'. The Maasai are allowed to graze their livestock in the reserve.

cau_hoi: The smallest country on the African mainland, shaped like a narrow strip along a river and almost entirely surrounded by Senegal, is which country?
giai_thich: Gambia is about 480 km long but only 20 – 50 km wide in places, running along both banks of the Gambia River. This peculiar border was drawn by the British and French during colonial times. According to a popular story, the border was determined based on the range of cannon fire from warships on the river, but historians still debate the details.

cau_hoi: The 'Horn of Africa', a peninsula jutting into the Indian Ocean resembling a rhino's horn, includes which countries?
giai_thich: The Horn of Africa is the easternmost point of the African continent, facing the Arabian Peninsula across the Gulf of Aden. This region has a strategic position on the maritime route from the Indian Ocean to the Red Sea. The climate here is often arid, with many areas prone to drought. Ethiopia in this region has a vast plateau, much cooler than the surrounding plains.

cau_hoi: What is the Sahel region in Africa?
A: A semi-arid strip transitioning between the Sahara Desert and the savanna to the south
B: The tropical rainforest region in Congo
giai_thich: Sahel in Arabic means 'shore', as this region resembles the 'coastline' of the Sahara desert. Sahel stretches from Senegal in the west to Sudan and Eritrea in the east, with low and erratic rainfall. Drought and overgrazing have led to desertification. African countries are implementing the 'Great Green Wall' project, planting a green belt across the continent to prevent desert expansion.

cau_hoi: The second highest mountain in Africa (about 5,199 m), an ancient volcano located almost directly on the equator, is which mountain?
giai_thich: Mount Kenya is an extinct volcano, with its sharp peaks being the remaining hard core after the outer parts were eroded. The country of Kenya is named after this mountain. For the Kikuyu people, Mount Kenya is the dwelling place of deities, so traditional houses are often built with doors facing the mountain. There are still a few small glaciers on the mountain, but they are melting rapidly.

cau_hoi: What is the official capital city of Tanzania?
giai_thich: Since 1973, Tanzania has decided to move its capital from the port city of Dar es Salaam to Dodoma in the center of the country, but the transition process has taken decades. Dar es Salaam (meaning 'place of peace' in Arabic) remains the largest city and economic center. Arusha is the gateway city to Mount Kilimanjaro and famous national parks.

cau_hoi: South Africa is unique because it has three capitals for three branches of government. What is the executive capital (where the president and government work)?
giai_thich: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative, where the parliament is located), and Bloemfontein (judicial, where the supreme court is located). This arrangement was a compromise when the colonies united to form the Union of South Africa in 1910. Pretoria is famous for its thousands of jacaranda trees that bloom in spring, covering the city in purple.

cau_hoi: The Ruwenzori mountain range on the border of Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which has snow and ice despite being near the equator, is nicknamed what?
giai_thich: Since ancient times, the Greek geographer Ptolemy wrote that the Nile River originated from the 'Mountain of the Moon' in central Africa, and many believe that refers to Ruwenzori. The highest peak is Margherita, about 5,109 m. Due to constant mist and heavy rainfall, the mountain hosts strange giant plants like giant lobelias and trees resembling aloes.

cau_hoi: How many countries in Africa are recognized by the United Nations?
giai_thich: Africa has 54 countries, the most of any continent. The newest country is South Sudan, which gained independence in 2011. Many borders between African countries are straight lines drawn by European colonial powers on maps in the late 19th century, not following geographical features or the distribution of ethnic groups, causing many issues to this day.

cau_hoi: Which country is the second most populous in Africa, with over 120 million people?
giai_thich: Ethiopia has the second largest population in Africa after Nigeria. Most of the population lives in the cool, fertile highlands at an altitude of 1,500 – 3,000 m, rather than in the hot lowlands. Ethiopia is home to over 80 ethnic groups and languages, and has its own script called Ge'ez, one of the few indigenous writing systems in Africa still widely used.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Madagascar?
giai_thich: Antananarivo is located on the highlands in the center of the island, at an altitude of about 1,280 m, built on many hills. The city's name means "city of a thousand people," according to legend, referring to the number of warriors who protected the city in ancient times. The people of Madagascar have mixed origins from Southeast Asia (from present-day Indonesia) and Africa, and the Malagasy language is very close to languages spoken in Borneo.

cau_hoi: Approximately what percentage of the world's population lives in Africa?
giai_thich: Africa has about 1.5 billion people, making it the second most populous continent after Asia. The population of Africa is growing the fastest in the world, and according to United Nations forecasts, by 2050, one in four people in the world will be African. Many African cities like Lagos, Kinshasa, and Dar es Salaam are growing at a very rapid pace.

cau_hoi: What is the southernmost point of the African continent, where the Atlantic Ocean meets the Indian Ocean by convention?
giai_thich: Cape Agulhas is located about 150 km southeast of the Cape of Good Hope. The name Agulhas means "needles" in Portuguese, possibly because sailors noticed the compass needle pointing almost directly north here. There is a sign marking the boundary between the two oceans according to the International Hydrographic Organization. The waters around the cape have many submerged rocks and storms, which have sunk many ships.

cau_hoi: The Nile River flows through (or has a basin covering) approximately how many countries?
giai_thich: The Nile River basin spans 11 countries: Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Kenya, Ethiopia, Eritrea, South Sudan, Sudan, and Egypt. Because many countries share the river's water, the sharing of this resource often causes tensions, such as the disputes between Ethiopia, Sudan, and Egypt over the large dam that Ethiopia is building on the Blue Nile.

cau_hoi: The Blue Nile, the branch that provides most of the water and silt to the Nile River, originates from which lake?
giai_thich: Lake Tana is located on the Ethiopian plateau at an altitude of about 1,800 m. During the rainy season, heavy rains on the plateau cause the Blue Nile to rise, carrying fertile red soil, which is the source of the annual flood of the Nile in Egypt. On the islands of Lake Tana, there are ancient monasteries of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church. Ethiopia has built the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) on this river.

cau_hoi: Where do the White Nile and Blue Nile converge?
giai_thich: In Khartoum, you can clearly see two differently colored waters flowing side by side for a while before merging: the Blue Nile is darker due to carrying more silt, while the White Nile is lighter due to containing more fine clay. The name Khartoum may mean "elephant trunk," referring to the shape of the land between the two rivers. From here, the Nile continues north through the desert to Egypt.

cau_hoi: Approximately what percentage of the Sahara Desert is covered by sand dunes (sand seas)?
giai_thich: Contrary to the familiar image of vast sand seas, most of the Sahara is a barren rocky plateau (hamada), stony plains (reg), rocky mountains, and dry lake beds. The sand seas (erg) only cover about a quarter, but there are dunes that rise over 180 m. The Sahara also has volcanic mountain ranges higher than 3,000 m, which sometimes have snow in winter.

cau_hoi: Which three countries share Lake Victoria?
giai_thich: Tanzania owns about 49% of the lake's surface area, Uganda about 45%, and Kenya about 6%. The lake has thousands of islands. In the mid-20th century, Nile perch were introduced into the lake to increase fish production; this predatory fish thrived but caused the extinction of hundreds of native small fish species, a famous example of the harm caused by invasive species.

cau_hoi: What is happening to the glaciers on top of Kilimanjaro?
A: They have not changed for thousands of years
B: They have lost most of their area in the 20th century and may disappear completely in the coming decades
giai_thich: Since 1912, the ice cover on Kilimanjaro has lost more than 80% of its area. The causes include warming climate and drier air, leading to direct evaporation of ice and less snowfall to replenish it. The image of the snowless peak of Kilimanjaro has become a symbol of climate change in Africa.

cau_hoi: What rank is Madagascar among the largest islands in the world?
giai_thich: Madagascar covers about 587,000 km², making it the fourth largest island in the world, after Greenland, New Guinea, and Borneo. The island separated from Africa about 160 million years ago and from the Indian subcontinent about 88 million years ago, leading to unique evolutionary paths for its flora and fauna: about 90% of the species found on the island are not found anywhere else. Madagascar is often referred to as the "Eighth Continent."

cau_hoi: What is the characteristic of the Harmattan wind, blowing in winter in West Africa?
A: Dry, carrying a lot of dust from the Sahara, making the sky hazy
C: Bringing salty air from the sea
giai_thich: From around November to March, the Harmattan wind blows from the Sahara southward to the Gulf of Guinea. The wind carries fine dust, reducing visibility, sometimes causing flights to be canceled, and humidity can drop very low, causing skin and lips to crack. However, the wind also brings cooler nights, so locals jokingly call it "the doctor" because it drives away the humid heat.

cau_hoi: Where is the point where the equator (0° latitude) intersects the prime meridian (0° longitude)?
B: In the middle of the Amazon rainforest
C: On the sea surface in the Gulf of Guinea, off the coast of West Africa
D: In the middle of the Sahara Desert
giai_thich: The point at 0°N 0°E is located in the waters of the Gulf of Guinea, about 600 km south of the coast of Ghana. There is only a weather buoy here. Cartographers jokingly call this place "Null Island" (zero island) because when geographic data is erroneous, many locations are mistakenly placed by computers at coordinates 0, 0. Africa is the only continent through which both the equator and the prime meridian pass.

cau_hoi: The tropical rainforest in the Congo River basin is the second largest rainforest in the world. Which one is it?
giai_thich: The Congo rainforest spans six countries, covering about 2 million km², and is referred to as "the second lung of the Earth." The forest contains vast peatlands, holding a massive amount of carbon. It is home to gorillas, bonobos (only found south of the Congo River), forest elephants, and the okapi. Millions of people, including hunter-gatherer communities, rely on the forest.

cau_hoi: Which country is home to Lake Volta, the largest artificial lake in the world by surface area?
giai_thich: Lake Volta was created when the Akosombo Dam was built on the Volta River in 1965, covering about 8,500 km², which is about 3.6% of Ghana's area. To create the lake, approximately 78,000 people had to be relocated. The dam provides most of Ghana's electricity. Beneath the lake are submerged forests, which are now being harvested for underwater timber.

cau_hoi: What is the highest peak in North Africa (approximately 4,167 m), located in the Atlas Mountains of which country?
giai_thich: Mount Toubkal is located in the High Atlas range, about 60 km south of Marrakesh. Climbing to the summit takes about two days, passing through villages of the Amazigh (Berber) people built from red earth on the mountainside. In winter, the peak is covered in snow. From the summit, on a clear day, one can see the Sahara Desert to the south.

cau_hoi: Which vast plateau is called "the Roof of Africa" due to its many peaks over 4,000 m?
giai_thich: The Ethiopian Plateau is mostly over 1,500 m high, formed by thick layers of basalt lava. The highest peak is Ras Dashen (about 4,550 m) in the Simien Mountains. The plateau receives a lot of summer rain and is the source of the Blue Nile River. Due to its cool climate and fewer mosquitoes, the plateau is much more densely populated than the hot plains surrounding it.

cau_hoi: What is the largest city in Nigeria, one of the most populous and fastest-growing cities in Africa?
giai_thich: Lagos is located by a large lagoon on the Gulf of Guinea, consisting of many islands and land areas connected by long bridges. The Lagos metropolitan area has about 15 to 20 million people. The city is famous for its "go-slow" traffic jams and massive markets. In the Makoko area, thousands of people live in stilt houses on the lagoon's water.

cau_hoi: About 95% of Egypt's population lives on only about 4-5% of its territory. What area is that?
D: Along the Nile River valley and delta
giai_thich: The rest of Egypt is a barren desert. The green strip along the Nile is only a few kilometers wide in the valley but widens in the northern delta. Therefore, this is one of the most densely populated areas in the world. Egypt is building new cities in the desert to relieve population pressure on Cairo.

cau_hoi: How many official languages does South Africa currently have?
giai_thich: In addition to English and Afrikaans (derived from Dutch), South Africa recognizes nine indigenous languages such as isiZulu, isiXhosa, Sesotho, and from 2023, South African Sign Language, bringing the total to 12. The isiXhosa language is famous for its "click" sounds. South Africa is known as the "Rainbow Nation" due to its ethnic and cultural diversity.

cau_hoi: In 2018, the kingdom of Swaziland in southern Africa changed its name to what?
giai_thich: King Mswati III announced the name change to Eswatini, meaning "land of the Swazi people" in Swati, to mark the 50th anniversary of independence. Another reason is that the old name was often confused with Switzerland in English. Eswatini is one of the few countries in the world with an absolute monarchy, located between South Africa and Mozambique.

cau_hoi: Which city is symbolized by a flat-topped mountain, often covered by a 'tablecloth' of clouds?
giai_thich: Table Mountain rises about 1,085 meters, with a flat summit stretching approximately 3 kilometers. When the southeast wind blows moist air up the mountain, clouds form and drape over the summit like a tablecloth. Table Mountain is part of an area with an incredibly rich fynbos vegetation, with over 2,000 plant species found on the mountain alone. Visitors can reach the summit via a rotating cable car.

cau_hoi: The annual 'Great Migration' of about 1.5 million wildebeests occurs between Serengeti (Tanzania) and which reserve in Kenya?
giai_thich: The herd of wildebeests, along with hundreds of thousands of zebras and gazelles, moves in a circular route of about 800 – 1,000 kilometers each year following the rains and new grasslands. The most dramatic sight is when they cross the crocodile-infested Mara River. This is considered one of the largest terrestrial migrations in the world.

cau_hoi: Which country in Africa is considered the birthplace of Arabica coffee?
giai_thich: According to legend, a goat herder in the Kaffa region noticed his goats jumping around after eating the fruit of a certain tree, leading to the discovery of coffee. Wild Arabica coffee still grows in the forests of southwestern Ethiopia. Ethiopia has a very elaborate traditional coffee ceremony, roasting beans, grinding, and brewing in a clay pot called 'jebena.'

cau_hoi: What is Chefchaouen in the Rif Mountains of Morocco famous for?
A: Almost all buildings and streets are painted blue
C: Home to the tallest mosque in the world
giai_thich: Chefchaouen was founded in 1471. No one knows for sure why the locals paint their houses blue: some say the color repels mosquitoes, others say it keeps the houses cool, or that blue symbolizes the sky and paradise. The winding blue alleys on the mountainside have turned this small town into a famous tourist destination.

cau_hoi: Kruger National Park, one of the largest wildlife reserves in Africa, is located in which country?
giai_thich: Kruger National Park covers approximately 19,500 square kilometers, nearly the size of Israel, and was established in 1926. It is home to the 'Big Five' (five large mammals): lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhinoceros. The park is working hard to combat rhino poaching for their horns.

cau_hoi: The volcanic archipelago of Cabo Verde in the Atlantic Ocean, off the coast of West Africa, was once a colony of which country?
giai_thich: Cabo Verde (Green Cape) consists of 10 volcanic islands, with a dry climate due to the influence of winds from the Sahara. The Portuguese arrived here in 1456 when the islands were uninhabited. Fogo Island has an active volcano, and the locals grow grapes and coffee right in the crater. The 'morna' music of Cabo Verde is very famous, especially with the singing of Cesária Évora.

cau_hoi: Lake Nakuru in Kenya was once famous for having millions of which birds gathering to feed, turning the lake pink?
giai_thich: Lake Nakuru is a shallow alkaline lake in the Rift Valley, where blue-green algae thrive, providing food for the lesser flamingos. At times, over a million flamingos gather here. In recent years, rising water levels have reduced the lake's alkalinity, causing many flamingo flocks to move to other lakes. Nakuru National Park is also a rhino sanctuary.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the wide strait between Madagascar and the southeastern coast of Africa?
giai_thich: The Mozambique Strait is about 1,600 kilometers long, with its narrowest point being approximately 420 kilometers wide. It features large whirlpools in the ocean and warm currents flowing southward. The strait has many small islands, such as the Comoros archipelago and Mayotte Island. Recently discovered large gas fields are located offshore Mozambique within the strait.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the highest mountain range in southern Africa, which forms the border between South Africa and Lesotho, meaning 'Dragon Mountain' in Afrikaans?
giai_thich: The Drakensberg Range stretches about 1,000 kilometers with steep basalt cliffs resembling a wall. The Zulu people call the range uKhahlamba, meaning 'barrier of spears.' In the caves here, there are tens of thousands of rock paintings created by the San people over thousands of years. The Maloti-Drakensberg area is a UNESCO World Heritage site for both natural and cultural significance.

cau_hoi: Which delta region in southern Nigeria is where most of the country's oil is extracted, but also heavily polluted due to oil spills?
giai_thich: The Niger Delta is one of the largest wetland areas in the world, featuring extensive mangrove forests. Since oil was discovered in 1956, Nigeria has become the largest oil producer in Africa. However, oil spills and gas flaring have polluted the land and water, severely impacting local fishing and agriculture.

cau_hoi: Which national park in Africa is unique for being located right next to a capital city, where you can photograph giraffes against a backdrop of skyscrapers?
giai_thich: Nairobi National Park was established in 1946, just about 7 km from the city center, with fences on only some sides. It is home to lions, giraffes, zebras, buffalo, and black rhinos. In 1989, Kenya burned about 12 tons of ivory seized here to send a message against ivory trafficking to the world.

cau_hoi: Which East African country did British Prime Minister Winston Churchill call the "Pearl of Africa" due to its beautiful scenery and rich nature?
giai_thich: Uganda is located on a plateau, bordering Lake Victoria, with a pleasant climate, fertile land, many lakes, rivers, mountains, and forests. Uganda is home to about half of the world's remaining mountain gorillas, living in Bwindi Forest. The Nile River flows out of Lake Victoria in the city of Jinja, Uganda, which has become a famous white-water rafting destination.

cau_hoi: What record does the Congo River hold compared to all rivers in the world?
A: It is the coldest river in the world
B: It is the only river that flows backward
C: It is the shortest river in the world
D: It is the deepest river in the world, with depths over 220 m
giai_thich: In the lower reaches, there are many rapids, and the Congo River's bed is carved to over 220 m deep. This extremely strong and deep flow creates "barriers" that separate fish populations on either side, causing many fish species to evolve separately even when only a few kilometers apart. There are blind, colorless fish living at the bottom of these deep pools.

cau_hoi: Lake Kariba, the largest artificial lake in the world by water volume, is located on the border of which two countries?
giai_thich: Lake Kariba was created when the Kariba Dam was built on the Zambezi River in 1959, stretching about 280 km. As the water rose, thousands of animals were stranded on the sinking islands, and a rescue operation called "Operation Noah" relocated thousands of animals to safety. About 57,000 Tonga people had to leave their homes to build the dam.

cau_hoi: What is the Dallol area in the Danakil Depression (Ethiopia) famous for?
B: Acid lakes and colorful sulfur deposits, resembling another planet
giai_thich: The Danakil Depression lies more than 100 m below sea level and is one of the hottest inhabited places on Earth. In Dallol, hot water from the ground carries salt, sulfur, and iron, creating brightly colored lakes and mineral columns with extremely high acidity. The Afar people mine salt by hand here and use camels to transport it for sale.

cau_hoi: The lowest point in Africa (about 155 m below sea level) is Lake Assal, located in which country?
giai_thich: Lake Assal is a saltwater lake in a volcanic crater, with a salinity of about 35%, saltier than the Dead Sea, causing the lake's shores to be covered in white salt crystals. The lake is replenished by seawater seeping through volcanic rocks from a nearby bay. Djibouti is located where three tectonic plates diverge, making it one of the best places to observe the formation of a new ocean.

cau_hoi: What unique geographical record does Lesotho hold?
A: It is the country with the highest "lowest point" in the world (about 1,400 m)
B: It is the lowest country in Africa
C: It is the country with the most glaciers in Africa
D: It is the country with the longest coastline in Africa
giai_thich: The entire territory of Lesotho is over 1,400 m above sea level, making its lowest point higher than that of any other country. More than 80% of the country is above 1,800 m. In winter, Lesotho experiences snow and even has the Afriski ski resort, one of the few ski resorts in Africa.

cau_hoi: The San people, one of the oldest ethnic groups in the world, have a tradition of living by hunting and gathering in which desert?
giai_thich: The San have lived in southern Africa for tens of thousands of years, possessing excellent skills in finding water and tracking animals in arid environments, such as extracting water from sand using reeds and storing it in ostrich eggshells. Their language features many unique "click" sounds. Genetic studies show that the San belong to one of the oldest lineages of modern humans.

cau_hoi: Why is the northern coast of Namibia called the "Skeleton Coast"?
A: Because there are many dinosaur fossils
B: Because the rocks here are white like bones
C: Because there are many shipwrecks and whale, seal bones along the coast
D: Because there is the largest ancient cemetery in Africa
giai_thich: Dense fog caused by the cold ocean current, along with strong waves and submerged rocks, has led to many shipwrecks along this coast. Surviving sailors faced a barren desert with no water. In ancient times, whaling and seal hunting occurred here, leaving many skeletons on the shore. The San call this area "the land God created in anger."

cau_hoi: Mountain gorillas, an extremely endangered species with about 1,000 individuals, live in the Virunga volcanic region bordering which countries?
D: Rwanda, Uganda, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo
giai_thich: The Virunga mountain range has cool, moist mountain forests at altitudes of 2,500 – 4,000 m. Scientist Dian Fossey studied mountain gorillas here for many years. Thanks to conservation efforts and eco-tourism, the number of mountain gorillas has increased from about 250 in the 1980s to over 1,000 today. Virunga National Park is the oldest national park in Africa (1925).

cau_hoi: Which country is the most populous landlocked country in the world?
giai_thich: Ethiopia has over 120 million people but has no coastline, as its coastal area was ceded to another country that separated in 1993. Today, most of Ethiopia's imports and exports must go through the port of Djibouti, connected to the capital by a railway line inaugurated in 2016. Finding a way to the sea is a significant issue for Ethiopia.

cau_hoi: What shape does the Nile Delta in Egypt take, and which letter is the term "delta" named after?
A: Square, named after the Latin letter
B: S-shaped, named after the Arabic letter
C: Triangular, named after the Greek letter Δ (delta)
D: Circular, named after the letter O
giai_thich: The ancient Greek historian Herodotus noted that the land formed by the Nile resembles the triangular shape of the letter Δ, which is why "delta" became the term for deltas worldwide. The Nile Delta covers about 24,000 km², making it the most fertile and densely populated agricultural area in Egypt. Today, the delta is shrinking and becoming saline due to reduced sediment and rising sea levels.

cau_hoi: What famous structure is located in Yamoussoukro, the official capital of Côte d'Ivoire?
B: The largest stadium in the world
C: The Basilica of Our Lady of Peace, one of the largest churches in the world
giai_thich: Yamoussoukro is the hometown of the first president Félix Houphouët-Boigny, who moved the capital here in 1983. The basilica was built between 1985 and 1989, inspired by St. Peter's Basilica in Vatican City. However, Abidjan remains the largest city and the location of most government agencies.

cau_hoi: Which is the largest country in sub-Saharan Africa by area?
giai_thich: The Democratic Republic of the Congo covers about 2.34 million km², nearly the size of Western Europe. The country is rich in resources such as cobalt, copper, diamonds, gold, and coltan (used in phone components), and much of its area is covered by rainforest. Congo produces most of the world's cobalt, an important metal for phone and electric vehicle batteries.

cau_hoi: Africa is the continent with the youngest population in the world. What is the median age (the age at which half the population is younger) of Africans?
giai_thich: In many countries like Niger, Mali, and Uganda, the median age is only about 15 to 17 years, meaning more than half the population is children. In contrast, the median age in Europe is around 42 to 44 years. A young population presents a significant opportunity for economic development if well-educated and employed, but also poses major challenges in education, healthcare, and job creation.

cau_hoi: What unique geographical feature does Africa have?
B: Crossed by the equator, the Tropic of Cancer, and the Tropic of Capricorn
C: Located entirely in the Northern Hemisphere
giai_thich: The equator runs nearly through the middle of Africa, with the Tropic of Cancer passing through the Sahara and the Tropic of Capricorn passing through Namibia, Botswana, South Africa, Mozambique, and Madagascar. Therefore, most of Africa lies in the tropical zone, hot year-round. The climatic regions in Africa are almost symmetrical: from rainforests at the equator to savannas, then deserts, and finally Mediterranean climates at the northern and southern ends.

cau_hoi: What did the Sahara look like around 6,000 to 10,000 years ago?
D: Green and lush with grasslands, lakes, and many animals like hippos and elephants
giai_thich: The "Green Sahara" period occurred due to slight changes in Earth's orbit that allowed monsoon rains to penetrate further north. Rock carvings in the Sahara depict people swimming, herding cattle, alongside giraffes and hippos. Beneath today's desert lie ancient lake beds and massive aquifers accumulated from this wet period.

cau_hoi: What distinguishes the Nile River from most major rivers in the world?
C: Does not flow into the sea
giai_thich: Most major rivers flow east or west, but the Nile flows from the East African highlands near the equator northward into the Mediterranean Sea. Therefore, the Egyptians referred to the southern region (upstream) as "Upper Egypt" and the northern region (the delta) as "Lower Egypt," which seems contrary to conventional maps. In the last 2,700 km, the Nile has almost no tributaries.

cau_hoi: What is the Siwa Oasis in the western desert of Egypt, near the Libyan border, famous for?
C: Salt lakes, freshwater springs, and date and olive groves in the desert
giai_thich: Siwa is located in a depression below sea level, where there are hundreds of freshwater and hot springs. The Siwa people speak a distinct Amazigh language, unlike most Egyptians who speak Arabic. The ancient houses are built from "kershef," a mixture of salt and mud. The oasis contains an ancient temple dedicated to the god Amun, where Alexander the Great once came to seek an oracle.

cau_hoi: What traditional feature are the Tuareg people, nomads living in the Sahara Desert, famous for?
A: Men wearing blue turbans that cover their faces, known as "the blue people of the desert"
giai_thich: The tagelmust turbans worn by Tuareg men are several meters long, dyed with indigo, covering their heads and faces while leaving only their eyes exposed, protecting them from sand, sun, and wind. The indigo dye often stains their skin, giving it a slight blue tint, hence they are called "the blue people." The Tuareg have their own ancient script called Tifinagh and once controlled camel caravans that traded across the Sahara.

cau_hoi: What is Lake Retba (Lac Rose) in Senegal famous for?
C: It is the deepest lake in Africa
D: The water of the lake is pink and locals harvest salt by hand from the lake bed
giai_thich: The pink color of Lake Retba is due to a type of microalgae (Dunaliella salina) that thrives in very salty water, producing a red pigment. The pink is most vivid during the dry season. The lake is so salty that people can float easily; salt harvesters apply shea butter to their skin to protect against the salt when diving down to scrape salt from the lake bed. The lake was once the finish line of the Paris-Dakar rally.

cau_hoi: Tugela Falls, considered by many sources to be the second highest waterfall in the world (about 948 m), is located in which country?
giai_thich: Tugela Falls cascades down from the Amphitheatre plateau of the Drakensberg range, through five consecutive tiers. In the dry winter, the falls can partially freeze. Some recent measurements suggest that the falls may be taller than Angel Falls in Venezuela, but this is still under debate. To reach the top of the plateau, visitors must traverse chain ladders hanging over the cliffs.

cau_hoi: Lake Turkana in Kenya, the largest desert lake in the world, is nicknamed what due to its turquoise water?
giai_thich: Lake Turkana is approximately 290 km long, situated amidst the arid lands of northern Kenya, with slightly salty and alkaline water. Algae in the water create the distinctive turquoise color. It is home to the largest population of Nile crocodiles in Africa. The lake's shores are where many important fossils of human ancestors have been found, such as the skeleton of the "Turkana Boy" which is about 1.5 million years old.

cau_hoi: Lake Natron in Tanzania is famous for which phenomenon?
A: The lake has tides like the sea
B: The water is very alkaline and hot, capable of "calcifying" dead animal bodies like stone
C: The lake has the sweetest water in the world
giai_thich: Lake Natron contains a lot of sodium carbonate from volcanic ash, with water reaching a pH of about 10.5 and temperatures above 40°C. Dead birds and bats in the lake are preserved in a mineral layer that looks like stone. However, it is also the most important breeding ground for lesser flamingos, as very few predators dare to approach. Bacteria in the lake give the water a red color.

cau_hoi: Sossusvlei, known for its giant red sand dunes and the white pan Deadvlei with its centuries-old dead trees, is located in which country?
giai_thich: Deadvlei once had water when the Tsauchab River overflowed, allowing acacia trees to grow. When the moving sand dunes blocked the river, the pan dried up and the trees died. The extremely dry air prevents the blackened tree trunks from decaying, standing tall for about 600 to 900 years. The nearby "Big Daddy" dune is about 325 m high, making it one of the tallest in the world. The red color of the sand is due to iron oxide.

cau_hoi: Fish River Canyon, one of the largest canyons in the world (about 160 km long), is located in which country?
giai_thich: Fish River Canyon in southern Namibia reaches depths of about 550 m, formed by the Fish River's erosion and the subsidence of the Earth's crust over hundreds of millions of years. The hiking trail through the canyon is about 85 km long and is one of Africa's famous trekking routes, only open during the cooler season due to the extreme heat of summer. At the end of the trail, there is the Ai-Ais hot springs.

cau_hoi: The Sudd swamp, one of the largest wetlands in the world, is created by the White Nile in which country?
giai_thich: The name "Sudd" comes from Arabic meaning "barrier", due to the dense mats of grass, reeds, and papyrus that once blocked explorers from navigating upstream on the Nile. The area of the swamp changes seasonally, potentially exceeding 30,000 km². About half of the water from the White Nile evaporates here. The Nuer and Dinka people raise livestock according to the swamp's flood rhythms.

cau_hoi: Mount Cameroon, the highest peak in West and Central Africa (about 4,040 m), is what type of mountain?
giai_thich: Mount Cameroon is located near the Gulf of Guinea and is one of the most active volcanoes in Africa. The western slope of the mountain receives moist winds from the sea, making the village of Debundscha at the foot of the mountain one of the wettest places in the world, receiving about 10,000 mm of rain annually. Each year, there is a grueling race to the summit known as the "Race of Hope."

cau_hoi: Chott el Djerid, the largest salt lake in the Sahara, where mirages often occur and where scenes from "Star Wars" were filmed, is located in which country?
giai_thich: Chott el Djerid covers about 7,000 km² and during the dry season, it becomes a hard, white salt flat with a road running straight through it. The hot air above the salt creates illusions of water in the distance. Nearby are the settings for the desert planet Tatooine in the "Star Wars" films. Some algae and bacteria give the standing water a pink, red, or green color.

cau_hoi: "The Eye of the Sahara" (Richat Structure), a giant circle about 40 km in diameter visible from space, is located in which country?
giai_thich: The Richat Structure appears as concentric circles, once thought to be a meteorite crater, but geologists have determined it is an uplifted rock dome that has been eroded by wind and water over millions of years, exposing different layers of hard and soft rock in circular patterns. Due to its size, it is difficult to recognize from the ground, so astronauts use it as a landmark when flying over the Sahara.

cau_hoi: The Qattara Depression, one of the lowest points in Africa (about 133 m below sea level), is located in which country?
giai_thich: The Qattara Depression in the western desert of Egypt covers about 19,000 km², consisting of salt flats and dangerous sunken sand areas that are difficult for vehicles to traverse. There has long been an idea to dig a canal to bring water from the Mediterranean Sea into this depression: the flowing water would turn turbines to generate electricity, then evaporate in the desert. However, the project has never been realized due to high costs and environmental concerns.

cau_hoi: "The Great Man-Made River" of Libya, one of the largest irrigation projects in the world, draws water from where?
D: From ancient deep aquifers beneath the Sahara Desert
giai_thich: The project began in the 1980s, consisting of thousands of kilometers of pipes with a diameter of about 4 m, pumping water from aquifers formed tens of thousands of years ago when the Sahara was still moist, delivering it to coastal cities like Tripoli and Benghazi. Since the ancient groundwater is not replenished, the extraction is like "mining water," and one day it will run dry.

cau_hoi: Why is there often dense fog along the Namib Desert coast but almost no rain?
B: The cold Benguela current cools the air near the sea surface, creating fog but preventing rain clouds from forming
C: Because there are volcanoes emitting water vapor
D: Because monsoon winds blow from the Indian Ocean
giai_thich: The cold Benguela current flows from Antarctica up along the southwestern coast of Africa. The cold air below and warm air above create a "lid" that prevents air from rising and forming rain. The fog that drifts inland is the main water source for many organisms in the Namib, such as a beetle species that can stand on the top of sand dunes to catch the fog. The cold current also makes this sea area very rich in fish.

cau_hoi: According to geologists, the eastern part of Africa along the rift valley is gradually separating from the rest to form which tectonic plate?
giai_thich: The African plate is splitting into two parts: the Nubian plate to the west and the Somali plate to the east, moving apart by just a few millimeters each year. In tens of millions of years, seawater may flood the valley, creating a new ocean, similar to how the Red Sea was formed. At that time, countries like Somalia, parts of Kenya, Tanzania, and Ethiopia may lie on a separate landmass.

cau_hoi: What is special about the traditional calendar of Ethiopia?
D: There are 13 months in a year and it is about 7-8 years behind the Gregorian calendar
giai_thich: The Ethiopian calendar has 12 months, each with 30 days, plus a 13th month that has either 5 or 6 days. Due to the different calculation of the birth year of Jesus Christ, the Ethiopian calendar is about 7-8 years behind the Gregorian calendar. The Ethiopian New Year (Enkutatash) falls around September 11 in the Gregorian calendar, when the rainy season ends and the yellow daisies bloom. Ethiopian tourism advertising once used the slogan "13 months of sunshine."

cau_hoi: The Makgadikgadi salt pans, one of the largest dry salt areas in the world, are remnants of a giant ancient lake in which country?
giai_thich: Makgadikgadi was once a super lake that could cover tens of thousands of km² in ancient times, now only flat white salt pans remain in the Kalahari Desert. During the rainy season, part of the pan floods with shallow water, attracting tens of thousands of flamingos to breed, along with migrating zebra herds. In the dry season, the salt surface is so flat that the horizon seems to disappear.

cau_hoi: "Copperbelt," one of the largest copper mining regions in the world, stretches across the Democratic Republic of Congo and which country?
giai_thich: The Copperbelt has rich copper and cobalt mines, exploited since the early 20th century. Copper accounts for a large portion of Zambia's export revenue, so the country's economy heavily depends on global copper prices. The demand for copper for electrical wiring, electric vehicles, and renewable energy is increasing sharply, making this region increasingly important.

cau_hoi: "Avenue of the Baobabs," the famous dirt road lined with giant baobab trees that may be hundreds of years old, is located in which country?
giai_thich: The Avenue of the Baobabs is located near the town of Morondava in western Madagascar, featuring about 20-25 Grandidier baobab trees that are approximately 30 m tall. These trees are remnants of a once-dense tropical forest, now surrounded by farmland. The sunset here is one of the most famous images of Madagascar. Madagascar is home to 6 of the 8 baobab species in the world.

cau_hoi: How many landlocked countries are there in Africa, the most of any continent?
giai_thich: The landlocked countries in Africa include Ethiopia, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan, the Central African Republic, Chad, Niger, Mali, Burkina Faso, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Botswana, Lesotho, and Eswatini. The lack of sea access significantly increases transportation costs, making trade more difficult. Therefore, rail and road connections to the ports of neighboring countries are very important.

cau_hoi: The Great Mosque of Djenné, the largest mud-brick structure in the world, requires the local people to replaster it every year, located in which country?
giai_thich: The current mosque was built in 1907, on the site of an older structure. The wooden poles protruding from the walls are not only decorative but also serve as scaffolding for replastering. Every year, after the rainy season, the entire town participates in the "Crépissage" festival to apply a new layer of mud. The ancient town of Djenné is a UNESCO World Heritage site, located in a seasonally flooded inland delta.

cau_hoi: The highest peak in the Sahara, Emi Koussi (about 3,415 m), is a volcano located in the Tibesti mountain range of which country?
giai_thich: The Tibesti mountain range in northern Chad is a remote, rugged volcanic area that few people visit. Emi Koussi has a crater about 12 – 15 km wide. Here, there are salt flats, hot springs, and sometimes snow falls in winter. The Toubou people live in this mountainous region, known for their survival skills in harsh desert conditions.

cau_hoi: Mount Nyiragongo, home to one of the largest lava lakes in the world, threatens which city in the Democratic Republic of the Congo?
giai_thich: Nyiragongo has very fluid lava that can flow very quickly: in 1977, the lava flow moved at a speed of about 60 km/h, the fastest ever recorded. The eruptions in 2002 and 2021 forced hundreds of thousands of people in Goma to evacuate. From the volcano's crater, visitors can look down at the bubbling red lava lake at night.

cau_hoi: The Simien Mountains in Ethiopia, a UNESCO World Heritage site, are home to which endemic monkey species that only eats grass?
giai_thich: The gelada monkey has a red heart-shaped patch of skin on its chest, lives in large herds of hundreds on grasslands at altitudes of 3,000 – 4,500 m, and sleeps on steep cliffs at night to avoid predators. The Simien Mountains feature cliffs thousands of meters high and strangely eroded peaks. There is also the Walia ibex, a rare mountain goat found only in Ethiopia.

cau_hoi: "White Desert" in Egypt is famous for what kind of landscape?
B: Pure white sand dunes like sugar
D: White chalk rock formations eroded by wind into mushroom and strange animal shapes
giai_thich: The White Desert is located near the Farafra Oasis in the western desert of Egypt. The chalk formations were created from the shells of small marine organisms when this area was once the bottom of the sea millions of years ago. Continuous sand winds have eroded the rocks into shapes resembling mushrooms, chickens, and lion heads. On moonlit nights, the entire area glows white like snow.

cau_hoi: The Tassili n'Ajjer plateau, famous for thousands of prehistoric paintings and rock carvings along with sandstone "forests", is located in which country?
giai_thich: The rock paintings in Tassili n'Ajjer, dating back about 12,000 years, record the climate changes of the Sahara: from a time with giraffes, elephants, and hippos, to the time of livestock herding, and then to the time of horses and camels. The sandstone pillars eroded by wind create a maze resembling a ruined city. There are also some rare ancient Sahara cypress trees remaining here.

cau_hoi: "Ténéré Tree", once considered the loneliest tree in the world because the nearest tree was about 400 km away, was what happened in 1973?
D: Chopped down by locals for firewood
giai_thich: The Ténéré acacia tree in Niger was the last remaining tree of a forest from the time when the Sahara was green, used as a landmark by caravans crossing the desert. The roots of the tree extend about 35 m deep to access groundwater. In 1973, a truck driver knocked down the tree. The trunk was moved to the Niger National Museum, and a metal "tree" was erected at its former location.

cau_hoi: The only country in Africa where Spanish is the official language, with the capital Malabo located on an island, is which country?
giai_thich: Equatorial Guinea consists of the mainland and Bioko Island in the Gulf of Guinea, where the capital Malabo is located. The country was a Spanish colony until 1968. Thanks to the discovery of oil in the 1990s, the per capita income increased rapidly. The government is building a new capital, Ciudad de la Paz, on the mainland.

cau_hoi: Which country in East Africa is known as the "Land of a Thousand Hills" and is famous for banning plastic bags since 2008?
giai_thich: Rwanda is a small landlocked country with a hilly terrain at an altitude of 1,500 – 2,500 m and a cool climate. Rwanda is known as one of the cleanest countries in Africa: tourists bringing plastic bags can have them confiscated at the airport, and on the last Saturday of the month, citizens participate in community service called "Umuganda". Rwanda is also considered the furthest source of the Nile River by some researchers.

cau_hoi: Which country has the longest coastline on the African mainland (about 3,300 km)?
giai_thich: The coastline of Somalia stretches from the Gulf of Aden down to the Indian Ocean, resembling the number 7 on the map. This maritime area has abundant fish resources due to the upwelling phenomenon bringing nutrients during the monsoon season. Somalia has a strategic position on the shipping route from Asia through the Suez Canal to Europe. Including the islands, Madagascar has a longer coastline.

cau_hoi: Which country produces the most cocoa beans in the world, the main ingredient for making chocolate?
giai_thich: Côte d'Ivoire produces about 40% of the world's cocoa, along with Ghana accounting for about 60%. The cocoa tree originated from the Amazon rainforest in South America and was brought to West Africa in the 19th century. Most cocoa is grown on small farms, and many farmers have never tasted chocolate. Belgium and Switzerland are famous for chocolate processing but do not grow cocoa.

cau_hoi: Botswana, the country with the largest population of African elephants in the world (about 130,000), has which famous national park along the Chobe River?
giai_thich: During the dry season, thousands of elephants gather at the Chobe River to drink and bathe, creating a spectacular scene. Botswana has rapidly enriched itself through diamonds after discovering large mines shortly after independence, using this revenue to build schools and roads. The country has also chosen a high-end eco-tourism direction, with fewer visitors but higher prices, to protect nature.

cau_hoi: Which country in Africa has the largest confirmed oil reserves on the continent?
giai_thich: Libya has oil reserves of about 48 billion barrels, the largest in Africa and among the top 10 countries with the largest reserves in the world. Oil accounts for a significant portion of Libya's export revenue. Nigeria is a major oil producer in Africa, while Algeria and Angola also have considerable reserves. Most of Libya's oil is located in the Sirte Basin.

cau_hoi: The ghost town of Kolmanskop, where desert sand has filled abandoned houses, was once wealthy due to the extraction of what?
giai_thich: In 1908, a railway worker discovered diamonds in the sand near Lüderitz (Namibia), sparking a diamond rush. Kolmanskop quickly had a hospital, theater, casino, and even an ice-making machine and tram. However, when richer diamond mines were found to the south, the town was abandoned from the 1950s. Today, the sand-filled rooms are a popular photography spot.

cau_hoi: The iron ore train in Mauritania, one of the longest and heaviest trains in the world (up to about 2.5 km long), runs through where?
B: Through the Sahara Desert from the Zouérat mine to the port of Nouadhibou
giai_thich: The railway line is about 700 km long, crossing some of the harshest desert regions. The trains can pull over 200 iron ore cars. Since there are no other means of transport, many locals and adventurous tourists prefer to ride for free on the piles of ore in open cars, enduring the daytime heat and nighttime cold for about 20 hours.

cau_hoi: Cabinda, Angola's oil-rich region, has what unique geographical feature?
A: It is an island in the Atlantic Ocean
B: It is entirely on high mountains
C: It is located in the Namib Desert
D: It is separated from the main part of Angola by a strip of land from the Democratic Republic of the Congo
giai_thich: Cabinda is an exclave, separated from the rest of Angola by a narrow strip of land where the Congo River flows into the sea, giving the Democratic Republic of the Congo access to the Atlantic Ocean. Cabinda produces a large portion of Angola's oil from offshore fields. This region also has dense tropical rainforests.

cau_hoi: The Etosha salt pan, covering about 4,800 km², meaning "the vast white place", is the center of the famous national park in which country?
giai_thich: The Etosha pan is the bottom of an ancient lake that has dried up, mostly consisting of cracked white salt ground throughout the year. Surrounding it are many waterholes where elephants, lions, black rhinos, and giraffes come to drink, making them easy to observe. In years with heavy rainfall, the pan fills with shallow water, attracting thousands of flamingos to nest. The white dust from the pan covers the elephants here, giving them a grayish-white color.

cau_hoi: The Tsingy de Bemaraha reserve, with its sharp limestone forests, means "the place that cannot be walked barefoot", is located in which country?
giai_thich: The sharp limestone peaks, rising dozens of meters, were formed when rainwater dissolved limestone along cracks over millions of years. Visitors must wear safety harnesses, walk on suspension bridges, and trails attached to the cliffs. Among the rock formations are deep gorges and caves with forests, home to lemurs and birds found nowhere else.

cau_hoi: Réunion Island (part of France) in the Indian Ocean holds the world record for what?
B: Most rainfall in 24 hours (about 1,825 mm in 1966)
giai_thich: Réunion Island has mountains over 3,000 m high that block tropical storms, causing massive rainfall. In 1966, the Cilaos area recorded about 1,825 mm of rain in 24 hours, nearly equal to the annual rainfall of Hanoi. The island also features the Piton de la Fournaise volcano, one of the most active volcanoes in the world, which erupts almost annually.

cau_hoi: Gabon is famous for having about what percentage of its area covered by forests?
giai_thich: Gabon lies on the equator, with most of the country covered by tropical rainforests, home to about 60% of the remaining African forest elephants. Gabon has established 13 national parks and is one of the first countries in Africa to receive international rewards for reducing emissions by protecting forests. In Loango National Park, hippos can sometimes be seen swimming out to sea.

cau_hoi: The Vredefort structure, the largest confirmed impact structure on Earth (about 2 billion years old), is located in which country?
giai_thich: When formed, the Vredefort structure was about 250 – 300 km wide, created by an asteroid about 10 – 15 km wide striking the Earth. Over billions of years, most of it has eroded, leaving only the rock dome in the center near the town of Vredefort. This is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Some scientists believe that the impact helped preserve the rich gold mines in the surrounding area.

cau_hoi: Why is the Afar Triangle region (Ethiopia, Eritrea, Djibouti) particularly interesting to scientists?
A: It is home to the largest glacier in Africa
B: It is the largest tropical rainforest area
C: It is where three tectonic rifts meet, and a new ocean can be observed forming on land
D: It is the only place without earthquakes
giai_thich: In Afar, the East African Rift Valley, the Red Sea Rift and the Aden Rift converge. In 2005, within just a few days, the ground in the Dabbahu region cracked open, creating a fissure about 60 km long and several meters wide. Most of the Afar region is below sea level, separated from the Red Sea by low hills; in the distant future, seawater may flood in.

cau_hoi: "Cape Floral Kingdom" at the southern tip of Africa holds what record?
A: It is the largest rainforest area
B: It is the smallest but richest plant kingdom in the world relative to its area
C: It is a place with no plant species
D: It is home to the tallest tree in the world
giai_thich: Botanists divide the world into six plant kingdoms, of which the Cape Kingdom occupies only about 0.04% of the land area but has around 9,000 plant species, more than two-thirds of which are found nowhere else. The characteristic vegetation type is "fynbos", consisting of small-leaved shrubs, protea (South Africa's national flower), and many orchid species. Periodic wildfires help many species to germinate.

cau_hoi: What dangerous phenomenon for ships is the warm Agulhas current flowing along the southeast coast of Africa famous for?
giai_thich: The Agulhas current is one of the strongest ocean currents in the world, flowing southward. When large waves from the stormy Southern Ocean run against the strong current, they are compressed and rise up, potentially creating waves over 20 meters high, damaging even large ships. The Agulhas current also brings warm water from the Indian Ocean into the Atlantic, affecting global climate.

cau_hoi: Off the coast of Le Morne Peninsula in Mauritius, there is a famous "underwater waterfall". What is it actually?
B: A visual illusion caused by sand and mud flowing down the slope at the seabed
giai_thich: From above, the flow of sand and mud drifts down the coral reef edge into deeper water, creating the illusion of water pouring down a chasm underwater. The water color shifts from turquoise to deep blue, enhancing the illusion. This is one of the most famous sights in Mauritius when viewed from a helicopter or plane.

cau_hoi: The Bodélé Depression in Chad is considered the dustiest place on Earth. What surprising role does the dust from here play?
B: Flies across the Atlantic Ocean and provides minerals like phosphorus to the Amazon rainforest
giai_thich: Bodélé is the bottom of a giant ancient lake that has dried up, covered with a layer of fine and light diatomaceous earth. Strong winds blow through the gap between two mountain ranges, lifting vast amounts of dust each year. Some of the dust crosses the Atlantic, falling into the Amazon rainforest, enriching the nutrient-poor soil washed away by heavy rains. This is an example of intercontinental linkage.

cau_hoi: The Fouta Djallon plateau is called the "water tower of West Africa" because it is the source of many major rivers such as the Niger, Senegal, and Gambia. Which country does this plateau belong to?
giai_thich: Fouta Djallon is a sandstone plateau in central Guinea, with high rainfall, many waterfalls, and grasslands. From here, the Niger River originates very close to the Atlantic Ocean but flows back deep inland. Deforestation and farming on the plateau threaten the water supply for many downstream countries.

cau_hoi: The Inga Falls on the Congo River is considered to have the greatest hydropower potential in the world. The "Grand Inga" project could produce approximately how much electricity?
B: About 40,000 MW, nearly double the Three Gorges Dam
giai_thich: At Inga, the Congo River drops about 100 meters over a series of rapids in a short distance, with a massive water flow. Currently, only two smaller dams have been built (Inga I and II). If completed, Grand Inga could supply electricity to a large part of Africa, but the project is very costly and faces many financial and political difficulties.

cau_hoi: In the city of Lokoja, the Niger River merges with which major river, forming a Y-shape on the map of Nigeria?
giai_thich: The Benue River originates from Cameroon and is the largest tributary of the Niger River. The two rivers divide Nigeria into three large regions, closely matching the areas inhabited by three major ethnic groups: Hausa in the north, Yoruba in the southwest, and Igbo in the southeast. The name "Nigeria" was proposed by journalist Flora Shaw in 1897, combining "Niger" and "area".

cau_hoi: What strange flow does the Niger River have?
A: Flows straight from north to south
B: Does not flow into the sea
C: Originates near the Atlantic Ocean but flows back inland towards the Sahara, then bends like a boomerang back to the sea
D: Flows in a circle back to its source
giai_thich: The Niger River originates in Guinea, only about 240 km from the sea, but flows northeast deep into the continent, creating a vast inland delta in Mali, then bends southeast through Niger and Nigeria, emptying into the Gulf of Guinea. This strange flow caused Europeans to take a long time to understand where the river originated and where it flowed.

cau_hoi: Lake Kivu, between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo, has what potential danger that concerns scientists?
A: The lake water is about to freeze
C: The lake's bottom contains large amounts of dissolved methane and CO₂, which could be released suddenly
D: The lake is about to be filled by desert
giai_thich: Gas from volcanic activity beneath accumulates in the deep waters of Lake Kivu. If an event such as an earthquake or lava flow occurs in the lake, the gas could suddenly surge, threatening about 2 million people living around the lake. To reduce the risk and harness energy, Rwanda has built a plant to extract methane from the lake's bottom for electricity generation.

cau_hoi: Ganvié, the largest floating village in Africa with about 20,000 people living in stilt houses on the lake, known as the "Venice of Africa," is located in which country?
giai_thich: Ganvié is located on Lake Nokoué. Traditionally, the Tofinu people established villages on the lake around the 17th – 18th century to escape slave hunters, as the beliefs of these hunters prohibited them from entering the waters. The residents travel by canoe, and there are floating markets, schools, and churches on the water. The main occupation is fish farming in areas where branches are planted under the lake.

cau_hoi: In 1986, a cloud of CO₂ suddenly erupted from a volcanic lake in Cameroon, causing about 1,700 deaths. What is the name of that lake?
giai_thich: CO₂ gas had accumulated from magma beneath Lake Nyos over many years. On August 21, 1986, possibly due to a landslide, a massive amount of gas erupted. Because CO₂ is heavier than air, it flowed down into valleys, suffocating people and livestock within a radius of about 25 km. After the disaster, scientists installed gas pipes from the bottom of the lake to the surface to gradually release the gas, preventing a recurrence of the disaster.

cau_hoi: Which country in North Africa has the largest phosphate ore reserves (the raw material for fertilizers) in the world, accounting for about 70% of global reserves?
giai_thich: Phosphorus is an essential nutrient for crops, with no substitutes, making phosphate very important for global food security. Morocco extracts phosphate from large open-pit mines and processes it into fertilizers for export to many countries. The phosphate here is formed from ancient marine sediments, rich in fish bones and marine organisms.

cau_hoi: The area around Lake Naivasha in Kenya is famous for which industry that exports to Europe?
giai_thich: Kenya is one of the largest exporters of roses in the world, with most being grown in greenhouses around Lake Naivasha, thanks to the stable climate year-round at an altitude of about 1,900 m. The flowers are cut in the morning and flown to Europe on the same day. However, the extraction of water from the lake for irrigation and fertilizer pollution has affected the lake's ecosystem.

cau_hoi: The blue-purple gemstone tanzanite is found in only one place in the world. Where is it?
giai_thich: Tanzanite was discovered in 1967 and was named by the jewelry company Tiffany after the country Tanzania. The stone is pleochroic: viewed from different angles, it can appear blue, purple, or burgundy. Because it is only found in a mining area of a few square kilometers, geologists believe tanzanite is a thousand times rarer than diamonds, and the supply may run out in the coming decades.

cau_hoi: In 2019, which tropical storm hit the city of Beira (Mozambique), causing massive flooding and over 1,000 deaths in Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Malawi?
giai_thich: Cyclone Idai is one of the most devastating storms ever recorded in the Southern Hemisphere. Heavy rains caused rivers to overflow, creating an "inland sea" covering hundreds of square kilometers in Mozambique. The city of Beira was about 90% destroyed. Scientists believe climate change is making such storms stronger and increasing rainfall.

cau_hoi: The Ubari lakes, green lakes located amidst the red sand sea in the Sahara Desert, belong to which country?
giai_thich: The Ubari lakes are fed by ancient groundwater that rises to the surface, surrounded by date palms. The lake water evaporates strongly, making it saltier than seawater, allowing swimmers to float easily. There used to be small villages by the lakes, but the residents have moved away. Due to groundwater extraction in the surrounding area, many lakes are gradually drying up.

cau_hoi: The easternmost point of the African continent is Ras Hafun, which belongs to which country?
giai_thich: Ras Hafun is a small peninsula jutting into the Indian Ocean, connected to the mainland by a narrow strip of sand. Archaeologists have found ancient trading port remnants here, indicating that this place traded with Rome, Egypt, and India over 2,000 years ago. In 2004, the town of Hafun was heavily damaged by a tsunami from the Indian Ocean, despite being thousands of kilometers away from the epicenter.

cau_hoi: The northernmost point of the African continent is Ras ben Sakka, near the city of Bizerte, which belongs to which country?
giai_thich: Ras ben Sakka is located at a latitude of about 37°20' North, further north than some regions of Europe such as Sicily (southern part), Malta, or Crete. The distance from the coast of Tunisia to the island of Sicily in Italy is only about 140 km. Tunisia is the smallest country in North Africa, with a long coastline along the Mediterranean.

cau_hoi: In 2012, the World Meteorological Organization canceled the record for the highest temperature in the world at 58°C measured in El Azizia in 1922 for what reason?
B: Because El Azizia is not real
D: Due to recording errors, inexperienced observers, and inappropriate measuring instruments
giai_thich: El Azizia is located in Libya. After many years of re-examining the records, experts concluded that the figure of 58°C was unreliable. Therefore, the world record was transferred to Death Valley (USA), with about 56.7°C measured in 1913. This story shows that scientists always recheck old data, even numbers that have been recognized for nearly 90 years.

cau_hoi: The Ahaggar Mountains (Hoggar) in the center of the Sahara, home to the Tuareg people, are primarily located in which country?
giai_thich: The Ahaggar range consists of ancient volcanic peaks and basalt columns resembling towers, with the highest peak being Tahat (about 2,908 m), which is also the highest point in Algeria. On the Assekrem plateau, there is a hermitage that offers a famous view of the sunrise. Due to the high altitude, it is cooler here than the surrounding desert, and frost can occur in winter.

cau_hoi: The semi-desert region of Karoo in South Africa is famous among scientists for what?
C: Fossils of ancient reptiles predating dinosaurs and a site for modern radio telescopes
giai_thich: The rock layers in Karoo preserve fossils of mammal-like reptiles that lived over 250 million years ago, helping to understand the origins of mammals.
